correctness.rationale: Kurz–Yaakobi's standard lemma forces any length-17 six-PIR code of dimension 8 to be a binary [17,8,6] code. The published optimal-code classification has exactly one equivalence class. For an explicit cyclic representative, the bundled verifier checks rank 8, primal minimum distance 6, dual minimum distance 5, all 34 dual weight-5 words, and the pair-incidence maximum 3. The proof then forces any six disjoint equal-syndrome recovery sets to have sizes (2,3,3,3,3,3), which would require five distinct dual weight-5 supports through the same pair, contradiction. The prior published upper bound 18 then gives equality. The package does not mistake the finite representative computation for the external uniqueness classification.

value.rationale: The result closes a named one-unit gap in the principal small-parameter table for P(s,k), rather than adding an arbitrary computation. The obstruction is structural: it converts the first unresolved length into a dual weight-5 pair-incidence condition in the unique optimal code. Exact small PIR block lengths are the central invariant of the anchor paper, and resolving a previously open table entry has direct reuse value for bounds and benchmark constructions.
